summary: This Docker Compose configuration sets up a service called 'app' that builds a Docker image using a Dockerfile in the current directory. It passes an SSH key into the build process both as a secret and by mounting the host's SSH directory into the container, allowing the application to authenticate with external services that require SSH credentials.

explanations.6: The 'secrets' section here makes the SSH key available during the Docker build process so the Dockerfile can use it without embedding it in the image permanently.
explanations.9: This passes the SSH key filename as a build argument, which the Dockerfile can reference via ARG KEY_NAME to know which key to use.
explanations.13: This mounts the host machine's SSH directory into the container's root user's home directory, making any SSH keys and configuration from your local machine available inside the running container.
explanations.16: This defines where the secret file actually lives on your host machine—in this case, pointing to your Ed25519 SSH private key file.
